en: Abu Ma'mar, Isma'il ibn Ibrahim al-Hudhali narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, he said: I said to 'Urwah: "How long was the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in Mecca?" He said: "Ten years." He said: I said: "Indeed Ibn 'Abbas says: thirteen years."

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and 'Abbad ibn Musa narrated to us, they said: Talhah ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Yazid, from Ibn Shihab, with both chains of transmission, the like of the hadith of 'Uqayl.

'Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to me, my father narrated to me, from my grandfather, he said: 'Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed away when he was sixty-three years old. Ibn Shihab said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed me of the like of that.

Abu Ghassan al-Razi, Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn Za'idah narrated to us, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adi, from Anas ibn Malik, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed away when he was sixty-three years old, Abu Bakr died when he was sixty-three years old, and 'Umar died when he was sixty-three years old.

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, and 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us, they said: Isma'il—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us; (H) and al-Qasim ibn Zakariyya narrated to me, Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to me, both from Rabi'ah—meaning Ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahman—from Anas ibn Malik, with the like of the hadith of Malik ibn Anas, and he added in the hadith of both of them: "He had a luminous complexion."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Rabi'ah ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahman, from Anas ibn Malik, that he heard him saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was neither noticeably tall nor short; neither extremely pale white nor dark brown; and his hair was neither excessively curly nor straight. Allah sent him at the onset of forty years of age, so he remained in Mecca for ten years and in Medina for ten years, and Allah caused him to pass away at the onset of sixty years, and there were not twenty white hairs on his head and beard.

Abu Kamil narrated to us, Hammad—meaning Ibn Zayd—narrated to us; (H) and Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to me, 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, both from 'Asim al-Ahwal; (H) and Hamid ibn 'Umar al-Bakrawi narrated to me—and the wording is his—'Abd al-Wahid—meaning Ibn Ziyad—narrated to us, 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Sarjis, he said: I saw the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and ate bread and meat—or he said: Tharid—with him. He said: I said to him: "Did the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ask forgiveness for you?" He said: "Yes, and for you too." Then he recited this verse: {and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women}. He said: Then I walked around behind him and looked at the Seal of Prophethood between his shoulders, near the cartilage of his left shoulder blade, like a gathered fist with moles resembling warts upon it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn 'Abbad narrated to us, they said: Hatim—who is Ibn Isma'il—narrated to us, from al-Ja'd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, he said: I heard al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid saying: My maternal aunt took me to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my sister's son is unwell." So he wiped my head and prayed for blessing for me. Then he performed ablution, and I drank from his ablution water. Then I stood behind his back and looked at his Seal between his shoulders, like the button of a bridal canopy.
Ibn Numayr narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, Hasan ibn Salih informed us, from Simak, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, he said: I heard Jabir ibn Samurah say: I saw a Seal on the back of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), looking like a pigeon's egg.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, that he heard Jabir ibn Samurah saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had graying hair at the front of his head and beard; when he applied oil, it would not be noticeable, but when his head was disheveled, it would be noticeable. He had a thick beard. A man said: "Was his face like a sword?" He said: "No, rather it was like the sun and the moon, and it was round. And I saw the Seal near his shoulder like a pigeon's egg, resembling his body."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abu Dawud, Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, he said: I heard Jabir ibn Samurah being asked about the gray hair of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). He said: "When he applied oil to his head, none of it was seen, but when he did not apply oil, some of it was seen."

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, Sufyan and Khalid ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, all of them from Isma'il, from Abu Juhayfah, with this, and they did not say: "fair-complexioned, having grayed."

Wasil ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Juhayfah, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with a fair complexion, having grayed; al-Hasan ibn 'Ali resembled him.

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abu Ishaq narrated to us; (H) and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu Khaythamah informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Juhayfah, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and this part of him was white—and Zuhayr placed some of his fingers upon his soul-patch. It was said to him: "How old were you on that day?" He said: "I was sharpening arrows and feathering them."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, Ibn Bashshar, Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi, and Harun ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, all from Abu Dawud; Ibn al-Muthanna said: Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khulayd ibn Ja'far: he heard Abu Iyas, from Anas, that he was asked about the gray hair of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). He said: "Allah did not disfigure him with white hair."
And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to me, 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, al-Muthanna narrated to us, with this chain of transmission.

Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-Muthanna ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, he said: It is disliked for a man to pluck a white hair from his head and beard. He said: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) did not dye his hair; the white hairs were only in his soul-patch, at the temples, and a few scattered hairs on his head.

Abu al-Rabi' al-'Ataki narrated to me, Hammad narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, he said: Anas ibn Malik was asked about the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) dyeing his hair. He said: "If I wished to count the gray hairs that were on his head, I could have done so." And he said: "He did not dye his hair; Abu Bakr dyed his hair with henna and katam, and 'Umar dyed his hair with pure henna."

Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to me, Mu'alla ibn Asad narrated to us, Wuhayb ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, he said: I asked Anas ibn Malik: "Did the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) dye his hair?" He said: "Indeed, he only saw a little gray hair."

Muhammad ibn Bakkar ibn al-Rayyan narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Zakariyya narrated to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Ibn Sirin, he said: I asked Anas ibn Malik: "Did the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) dye his hair?" He said: "He did not reach the extent of needing dye; there were only white hairs in his beard." He said: I said to him: "Did Abu Bakr dye his hair?" He said: He said: "Yes, with henna and katam."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Numayr, and 'Amr al-Naqid narrated to us, all from Ibn Idris—'Amr said: 'Abdullah ibn Idris al-Awdi narrated to us—from Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, he said: Anas ibn Malik was asked: "Did the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) dye his hair?" He said: "Indeed, he had seen only a little gray hair"—Ibn Idris said: as if he regarded it as very little—"and Abu Bakr and 'Umar dyed their hair with henna and katam."

'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri narrated to us, 'Abd al-A'la ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu al-Tufayl, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and there was no man on the face of the earth who had seen him besides me. He said: I said to him: "How did you see him?" He said: "He was fair-complexioned, handsome, and of moderate, well-proportioned build."

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, Khalid ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu al-Tufayl, he said: I said to him: "Did you see the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?" He said: "Yes, he was fair-complexioned with a handsome face." Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj said: Abu al-Tufayl died in the year 100 AH, and he was the last of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to pass away.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, he said: I heard Jabir ibn Samurah say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was wide-mouthed, ashkal al-'ayn (having wide eyes with reddish streaks in the whites), and lean-heeled. He said: I said to Simak: "What is dali' al-fam?" He said: "Wide-mouthed." He said: I said: "What is ashkal al-'ayn?" He said: "Long eye-slit (wide eyes)." He said: I said: "What is manhūs al-'aqib?" He said: "Having little flesh on the heels."

Yahya ibn Yahya and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, he said: The hair of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) reached the middle of his ears.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Habban ibn Hilal narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, they said: Hammam narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, that the hair of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to touch his shoulders.

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us, Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, he said: I said to Anas ibn Malik: "How was the hair of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?" He said: "His hair was wavy, neither crisp-curly nor completely limp, falling between his ears and his shoulders."

Abu Kurayb, Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Yusuf, from his father, from Abu Ishaq, he said: I heard al-Bara' saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had the most handsome face among people and the finest physique, neither excessively tall nor short.

'Amr al-Naqid and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', he said: I have never seen anyone with hair reaching the earlobes more handsome in a red mantle than the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). His hair touched his shoulders; he was broad-shouldered, neither tall nor short. Abu Kurayb said: having hair.
